Sam D: Hey team — we're seeing a flood of 429s on the embeddings endpoint when running our nightly bulk job. Started last night ~02:10 UTC, persistent. job size ~1.2M texts split into 20k requests, parallelism ~120, batch_size=512. Error: "rate_limit_exceeded" and sometimes "quota_exceeded". Headers sometimes include Retry-After: 60. Any quick mitigation? 
Marta (Support): Thanks Sam. Can you paste the exact curl or SDK call you use? Also do you see any logs showing per-request latencies or concurrency? 
Sam D: Here's the relevant curl we use (simplified):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input": ["... large array ..."], "batch_size":512}'
```
Sam D: We kick off 120 workers each sending batches of 512. Memory's fine, but we hit 429 after ~5-10 minutes.
Riley (Oncall): That's a classic burst-throttling scenario. Our hosted rate limits protect against noisy neighbors. Two immediate options: 1) add client-side rate-limiting + exponential backoff with jitter; 2) reduce concurrency and batch_size. Can you try concurrency=20 and batch_size=128 for a quick test? 
James (Infra): Also check that you're not mixing many API keys or clients from the same IP — that aggregates against a shared rate cap. If you're on a single ephemeral IP egress, it might be seen as one source.
Sam D: We're on a single CI runner cluster so yeah same IP. Trying your suggested knobs now.
Sam D: Quick test result: concurrency=24, batch_size=128 removed most 429s but a few remain with Retry-After: 30. 
Marta (Support): Good repro, thanks. Could you also paste the response body for one 429? Any fields like "limit_type" or "window" help. 
Sam D: Body shows: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"burst limit exceeded","retry_after":30}
Mona (Billing): fyi if it's quota_exceeded we may need to check plan limits — but sounds burst limit here. Sam, which billing account are you under? 
Sam D: Account datapipeline-inc@org, plan: Growth. 
Mona (Billing): Growth has generous monthly tokens but still enforces per-minute burst caps. For sustained high-throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated or a higher concurrency quota. I can flag a temporary uplift while you validate. 
Riley (Oncall): For immediate mitigation, implement this client-side backoff pattern (pseudocode):
```python
for attempt in range(max_retries):
  try:
    resp = call_embeddings_batch(...)
    if resp.status == 200: break
  except RateLimitError as e:
    wait = min(base * (2**attempt), max_wait) + random.uniform(0, jitter)
    sleep(wait)
```
Use the Retry-After header when present as a hint to set wait = max(wait, retry_after).

Sam D: Implemented. Re-run shows much smoother. Thanks. A couple followups: 1) why did 512 batches trigger more 429s than 128? 2) any server-side knobs to avoid hitting these with our workload? 
James (Infra): Larger batches mean longer token-processing time per request which reduces parallelism efficiency and can cause uneven load surges at shard boundaries. Also the runtime applies per-request concurrency limits and a token throughput cap. So higher batch_size increases per-request CPU/GPU time and raises the chance of hitting burst windows. 
Marta (Support): We can open a ticket to request a temporary burst increase while you migrate. Also we can advise on partitioning the job across time windows rather than blasting all at once. 
Sam D: That helps. Can you outline the minimal steps we should take to make our next run reliable? 
Marta (Support): Sure — checklist:
- reduce batch_size to 64–256 depending on average token length
- cap parallel workers so sustained qps < X (we'll compute for your account once you share avg token/sec)
- implement exponential backoff + honor Retry-After
- add jitter to avoid thundering herd
- consider spreading job over N minutes with a leaky-bucket token pool
- contact billing for temporary quota uplift or evaluate Dedicated

Riley (Oncall): I'll run a quick simulation against a staging capacity mirror and get back with recommended qps and target batch_size for embed-large-v1.
sre-bot: Simulation job queued (job_id=sim-99011). Estimated completion in ~12m.
Riley (Oncall): Simulation confirms safe steady qps ~180 requests/min with batch_size=128 for your data distribution. For your 20k requests you'd want to spread over ~112 minutes or request a temporary uplift.
Sam D: Got it — thanks all. Please open the ticket w/ billing uplift and any SRE simulation outputs.
Marta (Support): Done — ticket #SUP-4521 opened, assigned to Billing + Oncall. Attaching sample logs + simulation link.
Mona (Billing): Noted, I'm triaging SUP-4521. I'll propose a 30-day temporary burst uplift to allow migration. 
James (Infra): Also FYI if you move to Redwood Dedicated you'll get higher committed throughput and can reserve GPUs for faster wall clock time; we can share an estimate. 
Sam D: Appreciate it. Leaving this thread open while we validate the full run tonight. 
Marta (Support): Thanks — ping this thread with results or if you hit new error variants (401, 413, etc.)
Sam D: Will do. :thumbsup:
